memoryReview.lesson: Keep the battlefield comprehensible in overhead view and avoid the first-person tunnel HUD and heavy dark vignette which would hide tiny spells.
Avoid text-first parchment spreads during active play; reserve ink-on-paper only for between-round upgrade choices and results.

references.observation: Noita combines readable small pixel characters with strongly expressive magical particle interactions.
references.principle: Unexpected interaction outcomes must have visible causes and a readable payoff.
references.application: The duel uses pixel block bolts, shield rings, dash wakes and impact sparks triggered from deterministic combat events.
references.avoid: Do not copy Noita's caves, destructive physics or heavy effect noise which would obscure a competitive arena.

references.observation: Hyper Light Drifter gives tiny top-down combat figures a strong silhouette against richly designed ruined spaces.
references.principle: Silhouette and contrast should do more work than labels during a fast duel.
references.application: Give both wizards distinct coats, bright headwear, staff shapes and differentiated projectile tint on a dark mineral floor.
references.avoid: Do not borrow its cyan neon-tech aesthetic, character art or sword-centric combat pose.

references.observation: Eastward uses dense handcrafted pixel detail with layered lighting and cozy lived-in environments.
references.principle: Small, restrained scenic detail can make a tiny place memorable without requiring busy UI decorations.
references.application: Set the arena in chipped stone, varied grout, moss flecks, torch pedestals and small cracks around collision blocks.
references.avoid: Do not imitate its specific portraits, side-scrolling composition or plot-heavy screens.

concepts.medium: 400x620 low-resolution Canvas art for masonry and animated pixel-sprite-like wizard characters.
concepts.composition: Overhead rectangular courtyard with tiny opponents and two thumb clusters in the phone corners.
concepts.interaction: Direct movement stick, hold to fire and tap shield or dash; rune selection sits over the arena.
concepts.motion: Short projectile trails, fast dodge displacements and impact blocks illustrate every collision.
concepts.rationale: Selected because arcade mechanics and straightforward collision patterns suit a short deterministic duel.

concepts.medium: Vector strokes and node-linked rings inside one DOM/SVG interactive diagram screen.
concepts.composition: The rune circuit itself is the full screen, and combat remains a small preview on the edge.
concepts.interaction: Players drag links and activate circuits rather than directly steering two magicians.
concepts.motion: Propagation pulses move around wires and gradually illuminate connected nodes.
concepts.rationale: Too abstract for the early v0.1 product; interesting as an optional later builder visualization.

concepts.medium: Isometric 3D toy stage with physically sculpted figures, rendered in WebGL on device.
concepts.composition: Camera looks across a tabletop miniature arena with very low side-angle walls.
concepts.interaction: Swipe to orbit camera and tap targets while virtual buttons call spells.
concepts.motion: Clay miniatures squash, roll and bob after spell explosions.
concepts.rationale: Heavy setup and camera complexity would cost responsiveness and clear PvP aim on the first version.

selection.reason: A top-down pixel courtyard makes spell impacts and movement legible with a small deterministic ruleset and restrained controls.

rejected.reason: Rune visualization before real duel mechanics would become a decorative tech demo rather than a playable competition.
Isometric depth and camera control add cognitive load and visual production work before combat balance is proven.

tools.reason: The browser Canvas 2D API ships on target Safari and Chromium and supports exact low-resolution pixels without a CDN.
Local vector icon can be authored and shipped without external libraries, fonts, streaming textures or licenses.
Web Audio provides tiny user-unlocked feedback tones that remain under user sound settings and offline operation.

assets.role: The cached masonry composition gives the small courtyard tactile depth during a duel.
assets.acceptance: Every obstacle has legible solid walls, top facets, shadow and moss without hiding small projectiles.
assets.integration: background() rasterizes a deterministic low-resolution canvas once, then render() reuses it for every frame.
assets.provenance: Original in-app authored Canvas paint instructions, not scraped or AI-generated image assets.

assets.role: The authenticated PocketWorks account portrait, hat and MASKOT species control the pixel mage, and its rune-specific overlay changes with the equipped build.
assets.acceptance: Eight standard presets, three official MASKOT animal shapes and a drawn PNG/WebP keep visibly distinct coats and portraits; a profile swap appears between rounds, never inside a live fight.
assets.integration: The app uses avatar-profile.mjs for same-account Pocket ID/Pocket Social validation, then mage-art.mjs composes base appearance and rune gear in both menu and battle without changing collision.
assets.provenance: Original programmatically authored Canvas sprite shapes; existing account images are treated as user-controlled raster data and never injected as SVG or HTML.

assets.role: A single angular overgrown wizard hat emblem connects the app to its tiny battle characters.
assets.acceptance: Shows an identifiable pointed hat and warm torn-paper palette at a launcher tile scale.
assets.integration: Linked from HTML, webmanifest and PocketWorks app configuration for the standalone application.
assets.provenance: Original vector geometry, no downloaded artwork, fonts or licensing dependency.

risks: Wizard and bolt may become too small on a narrow phone.
Virtual thumb controls may obscure a spell near the bottom wall.
Three rune choices may overflow on a short iPhone viewport.
Owner-drawn artwork may decode slowly; retain guest sprite and swap only at a round boundary.
Large or invalid account raster must never freeze Canvas rendering or enter match storage.
Special rune armor must not conceal an otherwise recognizable animal silhouette.
comparisons: Compare home and fight screenshots at 390x844: background remains readable, menu hides cleanly.
Compare fight and rune-draft screens: choices appear above scene without vertical overflow.
Compare fight state to not-dead-yet and meat-exe: different view axis, text density and ability placement.
Compare frog/cat/rabbit profile preview vs combat sprite to verify both identify the same account.
Compare basic and armor/clone/heat rune builds: each adds features without erasing the original hat and ear outline.
